title: Partition Suit (Batwara Mamla) in Bangladesh for NRBs: How to Claim Your Inherited Land from USA, UK & Canada (2026)
metaTitle: Partition Suit Bangladesh: Batwara Mamla Guide for NRBs 2026
metaDescription: Exhaustive legal guide for NRBs in USA, UK & Canada to file a Partition Suit (বাটোয়ারা মামলা) in Bangladesh without travelling. Court fees, Saham shares & injunctions.
keywords: how to file partition suit from abroad bangladesh
saham share distribution civil court dhaka
heroIntro: For hundreds of thousands of Non-Resident Bangladeshis (NRBs) residing in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, and Australia, one of the most agonizing legal struggles involves ancestral real estate locked in family conflict. When a patriarch or matriarch passes away, resident siblings, uncles, or aggressive step-relatives frequently usurp prime road-front land, conceal rental revenues from commercial properties, or hurriedly attempt third-party sales while refusing amicable family partition. When informal negotiations fail, the sole definitive, enforceable legal remedy under Bangladeshi law is instituting a formal **Partition Suit (বাটোয়ারা মামলা)** under the Partition Act 1893 and the Code of Civil Procedure 1908. Crucially, an overseas heir does NOT need to sacrifice their employment or travel to Bangladesh to litigate. By appointing an attorney through a Consular Special Power of Attorney, an expatriate can freeze unlawful construction through immediate temporary injunctions, establish their lawful fractional share (Saham), and secure physical demarcated possession with police assistance.

quickAnswer.heading: Partition Suit for Expats: Core Procedural Roadmap
points: Execute a Special Power of Attorney abroad appointing an advocate or trusted representative to file and conduct the suit.
Obtain foundational family documents: Warishan Certificate, Death Certificate of predecessor, and all historical Khatians (CS, SA, RS, BS).
Serve a formal Legal Notice demanding partition by mutual metes and bounds within a 15–30 day window.
Institute the Partition Suit in the Senior Assistant Judge or Joint District Judge Court having local territorial jurisdiction.
Move an emergency petition under Order XXXIX Rules 1 & 2 CPC for an ad-interim temporary injunction to restrain illegal sale or construction.
Secure the Preliminary Decree (প্রাথমিক ডিক্রি) declaring your specific mathematical fraction (Saham / সাহাম).
Apply for the appointment of a Court Advocate Commissioner to physically survey boundaries, draw partition maps, and confirm the Final Decree.
Enforce delivery of physical possession through an Execution Case (বন্টন ডিক্রি জারী মামলা) backed by court Nazir and police personnel.

sections.h2: 1. The Legal Concept of Joint Ownership & Co-Sharership (সহ-অংশীদারিত্ব)
sections.content:
Under both Islamic jurisprudence (ফারায়েজ / Farayez) and Hindu personal law (Dayabhaga School), the death of a property owner instantly transforms the surviving legal heirs into co-owners in joint tenancy. Key legal principles that every overseas heir must understand include:

  • Undivided Interest across Every Square Inch: Until a registered deed of partition (রেজিস্ট্রিকৃত আপস বন্টননামা) is executed or a civil court passes a partition decree, no single heir owns a specific demarcated physical plot. Every co-sharer holds an undivided fractional interest in every square inch of the ancestral estate.
  • Illegal Unilateral Transfers: If a resident brother purports to sell the 'front 5 decimals' of road-facing land to a developer, the transfer is legally defective. Under Section 44 of the Transfer of Property Act 1882, the buyer only steps into the shoes of the co-sharer's undivided interest and cannot claim exclusive possession without a partition suit.
  • Constructive Possession: Possession of one co-sharer is legally regarded as possession on behalf of all co-sharers (সহ-দখল), unless an active, overt ouster has occurred.

sections.h2: 2. Statutory Framework: Partition Act 1893 & Code of Civil Procedure 1908
sections.content:
Partition litigation is anchored primarily in three statutory pillars:

  1. The Partition Act, 1893 (Act No. IV of 1893): Governs the judicial division of property among co-sharers. Section 2 of the Act provides that where property cannot reasonably or conveniently be divided into physical shares, the court may order a public or private auction among co-sharers, distributing the monetary proceeds. Section 4 allows a family member to buy out a stranger who purchased an undivided share in a family dwelling house.
  2. The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (CPC): Governs the pleadings, discovery, preliminary decree under Order XX Rule 18, appointment of commissioners under Order XXVI Rule 13, and execution under Order XXI.
  3. The Court-fees Act, 1870: Regulates the statutory stamp duty payable on the plaint depending on whether title is disputed.

sections.h2: 3. Grounds for Filing: Recognizing Co-Sharer Fraud & Ouster
sections.content:
Expats should never wait passively when family negotiations stall. Instituting a partition suit becomes urgent in the following scenarios:

  • Monopolization of Commercial Income: Resident relatives collect rents from ancestral markets, shopping complexes, or multi-story apartments and refuse to wire the expat's rightful share.
  • Unequal Physical Possession: Local siblings occupy high-value commercial frontage while attempting to relegate overseas heirs to low-value, water-logged, or rear-inaccessible land.
  • Attempts to Deprive Female Heirs: In many rural areas, brothers pressure overseas sisters to 'surrender' their shares or falsely claim an oral gift (Heba) was made prior to the father's demise.
  • Impending Developer Contracts: Relatives sign unauthorized Memorandums of Understanding (MoU) with real estate developers to demolish ancestral structures without your consent.

sections.h2: 4. How an NRB Can Litigate Entirely from Abroad (Order III Rule 1 CPC)
sections.content:
A prevalent myth is that an expatriate plaintiff must continuously attend court hearings in Bangladesh. This is legally untrue:

Order III Rule 1 of the CPC: Expressly permits any suit, application, or appearance in a civil court to be instituted and prosecuted by the party's 'recognized agent' or an enrolled pleader. An expatriate living in New York, London, or Toronto executes a Special Power of Attorney in Form 1 before the Bangladesh Embassy, completes MOFA and DC office stamping, and empowers their attorney to sign the plaint, verification, and affidavits.

The expat's physical presence is generally required only at the final evidence stage (examination-in-chief and cross-examination), and even this can frequently be handled through commission under Order XXVI or through short visits coordinated with counsel.

sections.h2: 5. Mathematical Farayez Share Distribution Matrix (Muslim Succession)
sections.content:
To claim your share, you must understand your statutory entitlement under Islamic succession law (ফারায়েজ). The following table illustrates fractional shares under standard Sunni Hanafi rules:

Surviving Legal HeirsStatutory Share of Mother/WidowStatutory Share of SonsStatutory Share of Daughters
Widow, 2 Sons, 2 Daughters1/8 (12.5%)Residuary: Each Son receives 2 parts (~29.17% each)Residuary: Each Daughter receives 1 part (~14.58% each)
Widow & Only 1 Daughter (No Sons)1/8 (12.5%)NoneFixed 1/2 (50%) + Residuary via Radd (رد)
Widow & 3 Daughters (No Sons)1/8 (12.5%)NoneShare 2/3 equally (~22.2% each) + Radd
Husband, 1 Son, 1 DaughterHusband gets 1/4 (25%)Son receives 2/3 of remainder (50%)Daughter receives 1/3 of remainder (25%)

sections.h2: 6. Step 1 — Serving the Mandatory Pre-Suit Legal Notice
sections.content:
Prior to instituting the suit, an enrolled Supreme Court advocate must issue a formal Legal Notice for Amicable Partition (বন্টনের আইনি নোটিশ) to all co-sharers via Registered Post with A/D:

  • Sets out the pedigree of the family (বংশলতিকা) and the complete property schedule.
  • Identifies the plaintiff's exact mathematical fractional share under personal succession law.
  • Calls upon the defendants to execute a registered Partition Deed (আপস বন্টননামা) within 15 to 30 days.
  • Warns that failure to partition mutually will compel the plaintiff to seek judicial partition, court costs, and an injunction.
  • Serving the legal notice is essential evidence proving that cause of action has arisen and mutual settlement was refused.

sections.h2: 7. Step 2 — Drafting the Plaint & Determining Court Fees (Fixed vs Ad-Valorem)
sections.content:
The plaint must be instituted in the court having territorial and pecuniary jurisdiction:

  • Court Jurisdiction: Up to BDT 15 Lakh = Senior Assistant Judge Court; BDT 15 Lakh to BDT 25 Lakh = Sub-Judge Court; Above BDT 25 Lakh = Joint District Judge Court.
  • Court Fees: Under Schedule II Article 17(vi) of the Court-fees Act 1870:
    • Constructive Joint Possession: If title is undisputed and the plaintiff claims joint constructive possession, a nominal fixed court fee of BDT 300 to BDT 1,000 is payable.
    • Disputed Title or Complete Ouster: If the defendants deny your title or have forcefully evicted you, ad-valorem court fees based on property market value (up to statutory ceilings, currently BDT 50,000 to BDT 75,000) must be paid.

sections.h2: 8. Step 3 — Securing an Injunction (Order 39 CPC) to Freeze Construction & Sale
sections.content:
The single most dangerous threat during litigation is defendants hurrying to alter the character of the land or transferring parcels to innocent third parties. To counter this:

Emergency Order 39 Petition: Simultaneously with the plaint, your advocate files an application for temporary injunction under Order XXXIX Rules 1 & 2 read with Section 151 CPC. The court must be satisfied on three criteria: (1) Strong prima facie case, (2) Balance of convenience, and (3) Irreparable injury. The judge issues an ad-interim injunction restraining defendants from alienating, encumbering, or changing the physical condition of the suit land until disposal.

sections.h2: 9. Step 4 — The Preliminary Decree: Adjudicating Title & Saham Fractions
sections.content:
Unlike ordinary civil suits, a Partition Suit proceeds through two distinct judicial stages:

  1. Summons & Written Statement: Defendants file their defense (Written Statement under Order VIII Rule 1 CPC).
  2. Settlement of Issues & Trial: The court frames issues regarding pedigree, legality of documents, and respective shares.
  3. Passing of Preliminary Decree: Under Order XX Rule 18 CPC, the judge delivers judgment declaring the title of the parties and their specific fractional share (Saham / সাহাম). No physical land demarcation takes place at this stage; it is purely a judicial declaration of legal ownership.

sections.h2: 10. Step 5 — The Final Decree: Advocate Commissioner Survey & Allotment
sections.content:
Once the Preliminary Decree is sealed, parties are given a brief window to divide the land amicably. If they fail, the plaintiff applies for a Final Decree (চূড়ান্ত ডিক্রি):

  • Appointment of Advocate Commissioner: Under Order XXVI Rule 13 CPC, the court appoints an independent Advocate Commissioner accompanied by a licensed government Amin (surveyor).
  • On-Site Physical Survey: The Commissioner visits the land after serving notice to all parties, measures the boundaries with modern GPS/theodolite equipment, and draws an exact allotment map (চিঠাকাটা নকশা).
  • Balancing Road Access & Valuation: The Commissioner ensures that every Saham receives fair road frontage, drainage access, and equalized property value. If one plot has higher commercial value, compensation adjustments (Owelty / ক্ষতিপূরণ) are calculated.
  • Final Decree Confirmation: The court hears objections, approves the Commissioner's allotment report, and seals the Final Decree.

sections.h2: 11. Step 6 — Execution Suit (জারী মামলা) & Demarcation with Police Assistance
sections.content:
If stubborn relatives refuse to surrender physical possession of the demarcated plot following the final decree:

  1. File an Execution Case (বন্টন ডিক্রি জারী মামলা) under Order XXI of the CPC.
  2. The court issues a Writ of Delivery of Possession (দখলনামা পরোয়ানা) directed to the Court Nazir.
  3. The Nazir, accompanied by police forces, attends the land, removes illegal obstructions, erects permanent boundary pillars (সীমানা পিলার), and delivers vacant physical possession to your attorney.
  4. Resistance constitutes criminal trespass and contempt of court.

sections.h2: 12. Real-World Case Study: UK Expat Securing His 3-Katha Share in Sylhet
sections.content:
Background: Mr. Joynal Abedin, living in Birmingham, UK, was denied his 3-katha share in an ancestral plot worth BDT 1.8 Crore in Dargah Gate, Sylhet by his two resident brothers. The brothers began constructing a commercial market covering the entire frontage.

Chamber Action:

  1. Executed an embassy-attested Special Power of Attorney appointing his cousin in Sylhet.
  2. Filed Partition Suit No. 84/2024 before the Joint District Judge Court, Sylhet, with an emergency Order 39 injunction petition.
  3. Secured an immediate stay order halting commercial construction within 7 days of filing.
  4. Proved title via original 1962 CS/SA Khatians and father's registered title deed. Obtained a Preliminary Decree declaring Mr. Joynal's 1/3rd share.
  5. Advocate Commissioner surveyed the land, carving out a dedicated 3-katha road-front commercial plot with independent egress.
  6. Final Decree confirmed, and physical possession delivered with police presence. Mr. Joynal is now developing his parcel independently.

faqs.question: Can I file a partition suit in Bangladesh if I do not possess original land deeds?
faqs.answer: Yes. An advocate can inspect Sub-Registry Volume Books to obtain certified copies (সার্টিফাইড নকল) of all historical deeds, as well as official certified Porchas from the DC office.

faqs.question: How long does a contested Partition Suit take from filing to final possession?
faqs.answer: An average partition suit takes between 2 to 4 years to complete both the preliminary and final decree stages in the trial court. However, protective injunctions are issued in the very first weeks.

faqs.question: Can my brothers sell my deceased father's land while I live in the USA?
faqs.answer: No. Under Section 44 of the Transfer of Property Act 1882, any sale executed without other legal heirs only conveys the seller's personal share; they cannot lawfully transfer your share.

faqs.question: Do married daughters have equal rights to claim partition under Bangladesh law?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under Muslim succession law, daughters inherit specific fixed shares, and have full statutory standing to institute an independent partition suit in civil court.

faqs.question: What is Owelty in a partition decree?
faqs.answer: Owelty is monetary compensation ordered by the court when physical property cannot be divided equally in value, requiring the party receiving the prime plot to compensate other co-sharers.

faqs.question: Can a Partition Suit be settled out of court through Solenama?
faqs.answer: Yes. At any point before the final decree, parties can enter into a Solenama (আপসনামা) under Order XXIII Rule 3 CPC, and the court will issue a decree based entirely on the amicable compromise.

faqs.question: What happens if the property is too small to be physically divided?
faqs.answer: Under Section 2 of the Partition Act 1893, if the property is indivisible (such as a tiny commercial shop), the court orders a public or private auction among co-sharers and divides the cash proceeds.

faqs.question: Does paying land revenue tax (Khajna) prove title in a partition suit?
faqs.answer: No. Dakhilas prove payment of revenue but do not establish substantive title. Title must be proved through registered deeds and unbroken Khatian records.
